findings.reason: §21's done-when should name the existing resolver it extends or deduplicates, which decides whether the new branch is a fix or a second implementation.
findings.text: §21 proposes a new report path for an unresolvable declared sha without citing the landed check-manifest resolver (`reckon/crew/reports.py:1526` `_commit_resolves_in`, used by `audit_manifest`) that already resolves and reports every named commit in the same `commits:` field

findings.reason: naming `reckon/crew/reports.py` as the owner to extend keeps one resolver and lets §21's report reuse check-manifest's, rather than deepen the fork.
findings.text: `_commit_resolves_in` is implemented twice (here, and `reckon/crew/promotion.py:477` atop promotion's `_commit_canonical_id`), so the "does this citation resolve" mechanism has two owners; §21 would extend the promotion copy for a field the reports owner already audits

findings.reason: the `/fleet` config dir is a different consumer from the systemd-unit path, so folding it in would widen §62 past the dependency-inversion defect it names.
findings.text: `config_directory` recomputes the same XDG_CONFIG_HOME-or-`~/.config` base that §62 is moving into a neutral module (`systemd_user_dir`), a second copy of the base resolution §62 exists to consolidate

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no remaining section introduces a module; §21 and §62 both extend existing owners, and §62 relocates a helper into the module that should own it rather than adding surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §21 extends promotion's citation handling while reckon/crew/reports.py:1526 (`_commit_resolves_in`, used by audit_manifest) already owns that behaviour, and promotion.py:477 is itself a second copy of that resolver.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §21 adds a report path in reckon/crew/promotion.py without citing the landed check-manifest resolver (reckon/crew/reports.py:1526 `_commit_resolves_in`, used by `audit_manifest`) that already resolves and reports every named commit in the same `commits:` field.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §61 lands the watcher on reckon/service.py's functions parameterised by unit name rather than keeping a parallel class with copied logic, which is the extension the item asks for; no unjustified wrapper is proposed.
